cohort: Women with a single viable pregnancy diagnosed with cervical insufficiency between the 14th and 24th gestational week without pPROM, clinical chorioamnionitis, vaginal bleeding, treatment-resistant uterine contractions or life-incompatible fetal anomalies
finding: Emergency cerclage between the 14th and 24th gestational week in the presence of cervical insufficiency (when signs of premature labor or infection are not present) is associated with a higher mean gestational age at delivery, longer time from diagnosis to delivery, and higher rate of term birth.
mod_finding: No difference in mode of delivery was found between the groups.
